candidates.computation_change_reason: The table is labeled MQL (method quantitation limit) rather than an effluent or discharge limit. Whether these µg/l values are enforceable compliance limits or only reporting/detection thresholds determines if reported measurements should be compared against them for exceedance under Purpose A.

The segment is indexed under section part_i but the on-page header references PART II. A different reading of which permit part governs this table could change which requirements are considered applicable for limit selection (A) and monitoring obligations (B), especially where other parts cross-reference each other.

candidates.locator: page 14, section part_i, table category BASE/NEUTRAL
candidates.computation_change_reason: This category header scopes which pollutants the listed MQLs cover. Interpreting whether BASE/NEUTRAL monitoring is required for all listed analytes, only when certain discharge types occur, or only under other unstated conditions in this excerpt could change which monitoring requirements are deemed applicable.

candidates.locator: page 14, section part_i, table category PESTICIDES AND PCBS
candidates.computation_change_reason: This category scopes a separate pollutant group with its own MQL schedule. Whether pesticide/PCB monitoring is obligatory, seasonal, event-triggered, or conditional on discharge characteristics affects which monitoring requirements are established as applicable versus not required or unresolved.

Representative numeric MQL entry with a relatively high value (50 µg/l). If MQLs are treated as compliance limits, the chosen interpretation of MQL versus enforceable limit directly changes whether a reported benzidine measurement is evaluated as exceeding an applicable limit.

Representative low-threshold MQL entry (0.01 µg/l). Interpreting this as a compliance limit versus a quantitation floor changes whether near-detection or reported trace values trigger an exceedance determination under Purpose A.

The revision date identifies which MQL schedule version is incorporated. If another permit section or later revision supersedes this table, a different interpretation of which MQL values govern FY2025 monitoring would change applicable numeric thresholds (A) and which monitoring parameters are in force (B).

*1 Default MQL for Mercury is 0.005 unless Part I of your permit requires the more sensitive
   Method 1631 (Oxidation / Purge and Trap / Cold vapor Atomic Fluorescence Spectrometry),
   then the MQL shall be 0.0005
candidates.computation_change_reason: Mercury is not listed in the table but is governed by a conditional rule tied to Part I and Method 1631. Whether Part I requires Method 1631 changes the applicable MQL (0.005 vs 0.0005) for limit comparison (A), establishes a method-specific monitoring obligation (B), and affects how missing, below-detection, or no-result mercury data should be classified when the effective quantitation limit differs (C).
